## Background

The Our World in Data website publishes research and graphics that provide insight into world data. We are going to recreate one of their charts and use it to practice our annotation skills.

If the thing you want to edit is not a theme element, then it is related to data and can mostly likely be changed inside a geom\_*() or a scale\_*() layer.

## Task

1.  Recreate [this graph](https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/excess-mortality-p-scores?tab=chart&stackMode=absolute&time=earliest..latest&region=World) as closely as you can. Add the United States, your home country, or another country of special interest to you (like where you served a mission) before downloading the data so you can complete bullet #4.
    -   The data is provided on the download tab.
    -   Focus your energy on labels, the y-axis, background color, and line color.
    -   Do NOT worry about making your graph interactive. Ignore that aspect completely
    -   If you are getting stuck matching the graph, try completing steps 2 and 3, then coming back to this step with the time you have left.
2.  Create a graph that highlights (draws attention to) any points that are above 100%. Be creative.
3.  Create a another graph that shows a different way to highlight/emphasize points that are above 100%.
4.  Add a line for the United States (or whatever country you chose), alter the chart to highlight/emphasize just the that country.
5.  Write a paragraph summarizing insights you gain from the chart. Also reflect on how you can use "highlighting" to help the data tell a story.
6.  Render the `.qmd` file. Push all files created as part of the render to your GitHub repository.

### Submit

In I-learn submit a link to the `.md` file on GitHub.
